content.comment_body: I'm preparing some training material and want to confirm a few things: - R stands for relay outputs - C indicates a real-time clock - E means Ethernet capability Are these correct? Also, do all current [product_name] modules with [version_no] include both the real-time clock and Ethernet by default, making these letters standard in model names? Thanks.

There's an additional letter: o (which refers to modules without a display). There are four types of [product_name] modules with [article_no]: - 230 RCE (relay outputs, RTC, Ethernet) - 24 RCE (relay outputs, RTC, Ethernet) - 24 CE (transistor outputs, RTC, Ethernet) - 12/24 RCE (relay outputs, RTC, Ethernet) For modules without a display, add an 'o' to the end: - 230 RCEo (relay outputs, RTC, Ethernet) - 24 RCEo (relay outputs, RTC, Ethernet) - 24 CEo (transistor outputs, RTC, Ethernet) - 12/24 RCEo (relay outputs, RTC, Ethernet)

analysis.insight_summary: Forum users are clarifying the meaning of letters in [product_name] model codes, focusing on the functions denoted by 'R', 'C', and 'E', and whether these are standard features in the latest [version_no] releases. Responses detail different module variants and note distinctions like display presence and output type. There is a clear need for straightforward documentation explaining product naming and available features.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect transparent and consistent model naming schemes along with easily accessible documentation explaining the significance of model code letters and built-in features. They anticipate all current [version_no] modules to include both the real-time clock and Ethernet as basic features.
